# Fixed: A manual import tied to a download that never completed no longer fails after importing

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. Reviewed in [#PR_NUMBER](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/pull/PR_NUMBER).

After a manual import, `ManualImportService.Execute` cleans up each download's folder and marks the download imported. It read the folder from the tracked download's import item, which only completed-download handling sets. A manual import sent with the download id of an item that handling never processed (one its client still reports as downloading, or one whose import failed) imported its files, then threw a `NullReferenceException`. The command reported "failed", the folder stayed, and the download was never marked imported. An unknown download id threw the same way, partway through the files.

- The folder cleanup and the Imported state wait for the client's Completed status, as completed-download handling does. An unfinished download's folder is still in use, and partial files don't count as audio: on `develop`, opening the manual import dialog on such a download could delete it. Imported would also end the tracking and let a client that removes completed downloads (SABnzbd, NZBGet, a blackhole) delete a paused or queued job with its data. An unfinished download (downloading, queued, paused or warned) stays in the queue after its files are imported, for completed-download handling or the user to finish.
- When the import item is unset, `Execute` asks for it as `GetMediaFiles` already does (`IProvideImportItemService.ProvideImportItem`). An import item that completed-download handling did set is left alone.
- Each folder cleanup is best effort. A failed lookup, or a path that is empty or not local (a remote path with no mapping), leaves the folder and is logged, and the other downloads in the command still finish.
- An unknown or expired download id imports the files without a download. The tracked-download cache starts empty after a restart, so such an id can still be a torrent that is seeding: in Auto mode its files are copied rather than moved. An explicit Move still moves.

Tests: `ManualImportExecuteFixture` uses the real `ProvideImportItemService` and folder-cleanup rules, with the download client and the disk faked; `FolderExists` validates the path as the real one does. A completed download with no import item has its folder cleaned and is marked imported. One still downloading, queued, paused or warned keeps its folder and state, even with only partial files left and every grabbed track imported, and the real `DownloadEventHub` with the next `ProcessMonitoredDownloads` never removes it from the client; a completed one is removed, as on `develop`. A queued download with no output path doesn't throw, and a completed one with an empty or unmapped remote path is marked imported without touching the disk. A failed lookup for one download doesn't stop the next, and an unknown download id still imports. `ManualImportUnknownDownloadFixture` runs the real `ImportApprovedTracks`: Auto copies the files of a download it can't find, and Move moves them. Every test but the import-item one fails or throws on `develop`, and dropping the status gate, the catch, the local-path check, the unknown-id check, the copy for an unknown id or the completed-download event each fails a test, as does finishing an unfinished download once its grabbed tracks are in.
